steps: Decide the job: find a %, increase, decrease, reverse, or compound.
To reverse, divide by the multiplier instead of multiplying.
For compound, raise the multiplier to the power n.
method_card.title: How to Work with Percentages
method_card.content:
Percentage of an amount: use a multiplier, or build from 10%, 5% and 1% blocks.

Increase or decrease: multiplier = \(1 + \frac{\%}{100}\) or \(1 - \frac{\%}{100}\).

Reverse: the result is 100% ± change, so divide by that multiplier.

Compound: \(\text{Final} = \text{Original} \times \text{multiplier}^n\).

steps: Reverse: the result is the original × multiplier, so divide the result by the multiplier to get back.
Compound: apply the multiplier once per year. For n years, raise it to the power n.
Growth uses a multiplier above 1; decay (depreciation) uses one below 1, such as 0.8 for losing 20%.

steps: Percent means out of 100. To find 10%, divide by 10; to find 1%, divide by 100.
Build any percentage from 10%, 5% and 1% blocks. For 35%: three 10% blocks plus a 5% (half of 10%).
To write one number as a percentage of another, divide them, then multiply by 100.

steps: An increase of r% multiplies by \(1 + \frac{r}{100}\); a decrease multiplies by \(1 - \frac{r}{100}\).
So +12% means ×1.12 and −15% means ×0.85. One multiply does the whole job.
To find the original from a known result, divide by that multiplier instead of multiplying.

gold.display: A house is worth \(£225\,000\) after a \(12.5\%\) increase. Find the original value.

guided_steps.say: A 12.5% increase means £225,000 is 112.5% of the original value.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the new value by the multiplier.

guided_steps.done: Adding 12.5% to £200,000 rebuilds £225,000, so the original was £200,000.

misconceptions.message: Taking 12.5% off £225,000 gives £196,875, but that is not the reverse. The £225,000 is 112.5% of the original, so divide: 225000 ÷ 1.125 = £200,000.

gold.hint: Multiply by 1.03 each year, or by 1.03 squared.

guided_steps.say: Compound means multiply by 1.03 each year. Two years is 1.03 twice, or 1.03².

guided_steps.done: Both routes give £4243.60.

misconceptions.message: Simple interest adds £120 twice for £4240. Compound interest earns interest on interest: 4000 × 1.03² = £4243.60.

guided_steps.done: Adding 5% to £26,000 gives £27,300, so the original was £26,000.

misconceptions.message: Taking 5% off £27,300 gives £25,935, but that is not the reverse. The £27,300 is 105% of the old salary, so divide: 27300 ÷ 1.05 = £26,000.

guided_steps.say: Multiply by 1.025 each year and watch for the first time you pass £5500.

guided_steps.done: Year 3 was £5384.45 (under), year 4 is £5519.06 (over), so 4 years.

guided_steps.done: Five fifths make 55, so 20% of 55 is 11.

silver.hint: Multiplier for a 12% increase is 1.12, then multiply.

guided_steps.done: The original plus the 12% is £392.
